basis: New fictional prompt-contained facts; independent of presentations and PDFs.
validationStatus: Validated on dev, stage and prod on 2026-09-28: all 25 chain answers correct in each environment; the complete load matrix returned 555 correct answers, plus nine correct preflight answers.

questions.question: What three types of goods does Aster Harbor Services transport?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medical supplies, laboratory reagents, and food samples.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Aster Harbor Services specializes in temperature-controlled transport of medical supplies, laboratory reagents, and food samples.

questions.question: When was Aster Harbor Services founded, and where are its headquarters?
questions.expectedAnswer: It was founded in 2019 and is headquartered in Portmere.
questions.sourceExcerpt: The company was founded in 2019. Its headquarters are in the fictional city of Portmere.

questions.question: Where are the three Aster Harbor Services transport hubs?
questions.expectedAnswer: Portmere, Lakeford, and Westhaven.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Its three transport hubs are Portmere, Lakeford, and Westhaven.

questions.question: What are the operating hours of the hubs and the customer care team?
questions.expectedAnswer: The hubs operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Customer care works Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 18:00 UTC.
questions.sourceExcerpt: All hubs operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The customer care team works Monday through Friday from 08:00 to 18:00 UTC.

questions.question: What are the three service plans, and what does the Dedicated plan provide?
questions.expectedAnswer: Essential, Priority, and Dedicated. Dedicated provides a vehicle and a route reserved for one customer.
questions.sourceExcerpt: The three service plans are Essential, Priority, and Dedicated. The Dedicated plan provides a vehicle and a route reserved for one customer.

questions.question: When are Essential shipments collected, and what is the booking cutoff for same-day Priority collection?
questions.expectedAnswer: Essential shipments are collected on the next business day. Priority shipments qualify for same-day collection when booked before 10:00 UTC.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Essential shipments are collected on the next business day. Priority shipments qualify for same-day collection when booked before 10:00 UTC.

questions.question: What are the maximum parcel weight and longest-side length for Priority shipments?
questions.expectedAnswer: 40 kilograms and 120 centimeters.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Each Priority parcel may weigh up to 40 kilograms, and its longest side may measure up to 120 centimeters.

questions.question: What temperature range is maintained for refrigerated shipments, and how often is the temperature recorded?
questions.expectedAnswer: Between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius, with a reading every five minutes.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Refrigerated shipments are maintained between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius. Temperature sensors record a reading every five minutes.

questions.question: Which portal provides shipment tracking, and what are the four shipment statuses in order?
questions.expectedAnswer: HarborTrack. Booked, Collected, In Transit, Delivered.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Customers track shipments in the HarborTrack portal. The four shipment statuses, in order, are Booked, Collected, In Transit, and Delivered.

questions.question: What does proof of delivery contain, and when does it appear in HarborTrack?
questions.expectedAnswer: The recipient's name, signature, and delivery time. It appears within 30 minutes of delivery.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Proof of delivery includes the recipient's name, signature, and delivery time. It appears in HarborTrack within 30 minutes of delivery.

questions.question: What information is required for onboarding, and how long does setup take after it is received?
questions.expectedAnswer: Company name, billing address, and primary operations contact. Setup takes two business days after all three are received.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Onboarding requires the customer's company name, billing address, and primary operations contact. Setup takes two business days after all three details are received.

questions.question: Who conducts each customer's service check, and how often?
questions.expectedAnswer: The customer's assigned account manager conducts a service check once a month.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Every customer has an assigned account manager. The account manager conducts a service check once a month.

questions.question: How can operational incidents be reported, and how quickly must critical incidents be acknowledged?
questions.expectedAnswer: Through HarborTrack or the 24-hour incident hotline. Critical incidents must be acknowledged within 15 minutes.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Operational incidents can be reported through HarborTrack or the 24-hour incident hotline. Critical incidents must be acknowledged within 15 minutes.

questions.question: When must an unresolved critical incident be escalated, and who receives the escalation?
questions.expectedAnswer: After it remains unresolved for 30 minutes, to the Duty Operations Manager.
questions.sourceExcerpt: A critical incident that remains unresolved for 30 minutes must be escalated to the Duty Operations Manager.

questions.question: How often does a customer receive an updated estimated arrival time during an active delivery delay?
questions.expectedAnswer: Every 20 minutes.
questions.sourceExcerpt: During an active delivery delay, the customer receives an updated estimated arrival time every 20 minutes.

questions.question: How far in advance must a planned route change be requested, and who approves it?
questions.expectedAnswer: At least 48 hours before collection; the Routing Coordinator approves it.
questions.sourceExcerpt: A planned route change must be requested at least 48 hours before collection and approved by the Routing Coordinator.

questions.question: Where is the backup dispatch center, and how quickly must it be activated after the primary center becomes unavailable?
questions.expectedAnswer: At the Lakeford hub, within 45 minutes.
questions.sourceExcerpt: The backup dispatch center is at the Lakeford hub. It must be activated within 45 minutes after the primary dispatch center becomes unavailable.

questions.question: Who calibrates the temperature sensors, and how often?
questions.expectedAnswer: Fleet Engineering, every 90 days.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Fleet Engineering calibrates temperature sensors every 90 days.

questions.question: When do drivers first complete cold-chain handling training, and how often do they repeat it?
questions.expectedAnswer: Before their first route, then every six months.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Drivers complete cold-chain handling training before their first route and repeat it every six months.

questions.question: What containers and seals are used for standard packaging?
questions.expectedAnswer: Reusable insulated containers with tamper-evident seals.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Standard packaging consists of reusable insulated containers fitted with tamper-evident seals.

questions.question: How long are standard shipment records and incident records retained?
questions.expectedAnswer: Standard shipment records: 180 days. Incident records: two years.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Standard shipment records are retained for 180 days. Incident records are retained for two years.

questions.question: When is the weekly operations report published, and which three counts does it contain?
questions.expectedAnswer: Every Monday at 09:00 UTC. Delivered shipments, on-time deliveries, and temperature excursions.
questions.sourceExcerpt: The weekly operations report is published every Monday at 09:00 UTC. It contains the number of delivered shipments, the number of on-time deliveries, and the number of temperature excursions.

questions.question: How often do customer service reviews take place, and which three metrics do they assess?
questions.expectedAnswer: Quarterly. The on-time delivery rate, temperature excursions, and mean incident resolution time.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Customer service reviews take place quarterly. They assess the on-time delivery rate, temperature excursions, and mean incident resolution time.

questions.question: Who reviews suppliers, how often, and against which three criteria?
questions.expectedAnswer: The Quality team, every 12 months. Delivery reliability, temperature safety, and completeness of documentation.
questions.sourceExcerpt: The Quality team reviews suppliers every 12 months. It assesses delivery reliability, temperature safety, and completeness of documentation.

questions.question: In which months are business continuity drills held, who leads them, and when must findings be reviewed?
questions.expectedAnswer: March and September; the Head of Operations; within ten business days after each drill.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Business continuity drills take place in March and September. The Head of Operations leads them, and findings must be reviewed within ten business days after each drill.
